properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 10 at 11:00AM EDT until October 11 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip
currents. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of
6 to 8 feet expected in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Hatteras Island beaches, and Ocracoke Island beaches.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, until 8 PM EDT this
evening. For the High Surf Advisory, from 8 PM this evening to
8 PM EDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The most likely time for strong rip
currents to occur is a couple hours either side of low tide,
which will occur around 2:00 PM Saturday.
properties.instruction:
Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Life-threatening rip currents. If caught in a rip current, remain
calm. Swim in a direction following the shoreline. If tired,
float or tread water until out of the rip current. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 10 at 11:00AM EDT until October 10 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and strong longshore currents in
the surf zone.

* WHERE...Crystal Coast beaches.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM EDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water. Strong longshore currents will
create dangerous swimming conditions.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The most likely time for strong rip
currents to occur is a couple hours either side of low tide,
which will occur around 2:00 PM Saturday.
properties.instruction:
Life-threatening rip currents. If caught in a rip current, remain
calm. Swim in a direction following the shoreline. If tired,
float or tread water until out of the rip current. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

Strong longshore currents can sweep swimmers and surfers into rip
currents, piers, jetties and other hazardous areas. In many
cases, the longshore current is strong enough to prevent swimmers
from being able to keep their feet on the bottom making it
difficult to return to shore.

properties.areaDesc: Haywood, NC
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 10 at 10:57AM EDT until October 12 at 2:00AM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
...The Flood Advisory continues for the following rivers in North
Carolina...

Pigeon River At above Old River Rd (NC 215), 1 SW Canton affecting
Haywood County.

.Tropical rainfall will continue to overspread the mountains through
tonight and become heavier. Storm-total rainfall of 4-8 inches is
expected, with isolated higher amounts possible across the upper
Pigeon River watershed upstream of Canton.  The highest totals will
occur along the Pisgah ridge and in the Shining Rock and Middle Prong
Wilderness areas within the headwaters of the east and west forks of
the Pigeon River.  There remains enough confidence that  out-of-bank
conditions are likely for the Pigeon River.  This rise above Action
Stage will result in nuisance, relatively shallow flooding of
low-lying areas adjacent to the Pigeon River, including farmland,
woodlands, low-lying secondary roads, greenways, parks, and other
flood-prone locations.

More significant rises along the Pigeon River are possible, and those
with interests along the river are encouraged to stay weather aware
and up-to-date on the latest stream levels and forecasts at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/GSP.  Current reasonable worst-case
scenarios are posted in the ADDITIONAL DETAILS sections below.
Forecast crests above Minor Flood Stage may result in the River Flood
Advisories being upgraded to River Flood Warnings.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Pigeon River at above Old River Rd (NC 215), 1 SW Canton.

* WHEN...Until late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...At 8.0 feet, Action/Advisory Stage.  Common, nuisance
flooding of low-lying areas adjacent to the Pigeon River is
beginning.  Floodwaters are beginning to impact farmland,
woodlands, nurseries, parks, athletic fields, golf courses,
greenways, and boat-access areas with up to 2 feet of inundation.
Low-water crossings may be inundated with up to 2 feet of
floodwater and become impassable.  Adjacent campgrounds, mobile
home/RV parks, and secondary roads may experience floodwater
inundation of up to 1 foot.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:45 AM EDT Saturday the stage was 1.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 10.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 8.5 feet
tomorrow morning.  The reasonable worst-case crest would be
around the minor flood stage of 10 feet.
- Action stage is 8.0 feet.
- Flood stage is 10.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 10 at 9:41AM CDT until October 12 at 6:00PM CDT by NWS Mobile AL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

Big Coldwater Creek Near Milton affecting Okaloosa and Santa Rosa
Counties.

For the Big Coldwater Creek...including Milton, Harold...Minor
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Big Coldwater Creek near Milton.

* WHEN...Until Monday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 10.0 feet, Flooding of lowlands and some fish camps
will occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:00 AM CDT Saturday the stage was 6.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage this
evening to a crest of 11.4 feet tomorrow morning. It will then
fall below flood stage early Monday afternoon.
- Flood stage is 10.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/mob. Click on
the Rivers and Lakes menu for forecasts and observations.

The next statement will be issued when updates occur.

properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued October 10 at 10:38AM EDT until October 10 at 12:45PM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
SMWTAE

The National Weather Service in Tallahassee has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Apalachee Bay or Coastal Waters From Keaton Beach to Ochlockonee
River Fl out to 20 Nm...
Coastal Waters From  Ochlockonee River to Apalachicola FL out to 20
Nm...
Coastal waters from  Suwannee River to Keaton Beach out 20 NM...
Waters from Mexico Beach to Apalachicola FL from 20 to 60 NM...
Waters from Suwannee River to Apalachicola FL from 20 to 60 NM...

* Until 1245 PM EDT/1145 AM CDT/.

* At 1038 AM EDT/938 AM CDT/, severe thunderstorms capable of
producing waterspouts were located along a line extending from 25
nm northeast of Buckeye Reef to 31 nm south of S Tower, moving
northeast at 20 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats...damage
vessels...and create suddenly higher waves. Make sure all
on board are in a secure location and wearing life
jackets. Expect wind gusts in excess of 34
knots...suddenly higher waves...frequent lightning...and
heavy downpours. Make sure all on board are wearing life
jackets.

* Locations impacted include...
V Tower and Buckeye Reef.
properties.instruction:
Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

to 60 NM...

properties.areaDesc: Kenedy Island; Willacy Island; Cameron Island
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 10 at 9:30AM CDT until October 11 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS Brownsville TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding. For
the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 3 to 5 feet in
the surf zone.

* WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island
Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through Sunday evening.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 7 AM CDT Monday. For the
High Surf Advisory, until 7 PM CDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding is expected, with water reaching
or pushing into the dunes on South Padre Island. Vehicles,
except those with four wheel drive and high wheel bases, will
be unable to be driven on the beach. This includes locations
north of Public Beach Access #3. Minor to moderate beach
erosion is expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions
and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the
best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.
